brief.situation: You are the ML engineer at Brisk Pay, a fictional payments company. At 11:00 a teammate deployed fraud model v9 to the production endpoint fraud-ep, meaning to canary it at 10%, but the deploy command set its traffic to 100%. Since then the share of payments blocked as fraud rose from 0.8% to 6.4%, almost all of them good customers. The lunch peak starts at 12:00.
handover: Model v8 is still deployed on fraud-ep with 0% traffic; it has been stable for two months.
The release plan for v9: 10% canary for two days, compared on precision at the fixed threshold.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the endpoint, the two deployed model versions and how traffic is split between them.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why good payments were blocked, what you changed, and how the next rollout is protected.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Connects the block rate to the split.
parts.modelAnswer: The 11:00 deploy used --traffic-split=0=100, so v9 took all traffic. v9's scores sit higher (median 0.41 vs 0.12) at the same 0.35 threshold, and the block rate went from 0.8% to 6.4%.

parts.label: Change
parts.modelAnswer: Split 90% to v8 and 10% to v9, as the release plan intended. Clearing the split would have stopped the endpoint taking any traffic; more replicas change nothing.

parts.label: Protected
parts.modelAnswer: The pipeline now sets the canary split explicitly and refuses 0=100 for this endpoint, and a per-model block-rate alert pages within minutes.

scoring.modelReasoning: The new model took all of the endpoint's traffic by mistake, and at the shared threshold it blocks many more good payments. The old model is still deployed, so set the traffic split back to the planned canary, 90% old and 10% new, and check the block rate. Clearing the split stops the endpoint taking traffic at all; more replicas serve the same bad predictions. Then alert per model and make the pipeline set the canary explicitly.
